source.title: Training Neural Networks for and by Interpolation
source.authors: Leonard Berrada; Andrew Zisserman; M. P. Kumar

record.tranche_reason: The study reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label tasks, but does not measure the claim’s training-versus-test generalization gap or any other listed version’s outcome. Its optimizer results are relevant only as performance context, not as tests of V1–V8.
record.gate_note: No qualifying rows: the study compares optimization methods using test accuracy and training objective, but reports no paired train/test error gaps, random-label memorization comparisons, width sweep, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison, large-batch penalty test, dropout intervention, sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal. Optimizer test-accuracy values do not establish V4 as framed because the reported evidence does not compare matched training and held-out performance or isolate adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under its stated tuning condition. The cited Wilson et al. optimizer-generalization claim is prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares optimizers' held-out accuracy on image and language tasks, bearing on V4. Paired training and test errors are not required for V4's held-out-performance claim. Tuning includes some regularization and batch-size choices, so these experiments do not exactly reproduce its learning-rate-only tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly describes ALI-G's competitive performance and reduced tuning, but incorrectly denies a conclusion about optimizer generalization. The authors explicitly conclude that ALI-G offers generalization comparable to scheduled SGD while requiring significantly less tuning, and report that it outperforms popular adaptive methods.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates ALI-G, an adaptive learning-rate optimizer; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed versions.

fits_no_version.finding: DNC final training objectives, CIFAR-100 training-objective comparisons, and ImageNet training objective/top-5 training accuracy measure optimization performance without corresponding held-out comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ALI-G can optimize interpolating models effectively with little learning-rate tuning.

record.problems: The experiments primarily report final test accuracy or training objective, rather than paired training and test errors needed to assess a generalization gap. Some baseline results are reused from cited work; CIFAR results are averaged over three runs with standard deviations reported.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Matched training performance for the reported test-accuracy comparisons; strictly learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning; broad optimizer tuning; switching Adam to SGD; word-level language modeling. Section 5.5 uses a different training protocol and cannot establish matched training performance for Table 3.
Controlled large- versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epochs and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Memorized-example removal and subsequent test-accuracy changes.

missing.what: Optimizer test-accuracy comparisons: SGD 98.3%, Adam/AMSGrad 97.9%, Adagrad 98.0%, L4 Adam 98.2%, L4 Mom 19.6%, and ALI-G 98.1%. Record the learning-rate, regularization, momentum and fixed-epoch conditions. Exclude SGD† as an externally reported result.

Four reproduced CIFAR comparisons, ordered WRN10/DN10/WRN100/DN100: SGD 95.3/95.1/77.8/76.3; AMSGrad 90.8/91.7/68.7/69.4; AdamW 92.1/92.6/69.6/69.5; Yogi 91.2/92.1/68.7/69.6; L4 Adam 90.5/90.8/61.7/60.5; L4 Mom 91.6/91.9/61.4/62.6. Include Table 6 uncertainties and the batch-size/regularization tuning conditions; exclude external SGD†.

ALI-G's comparable held-out performance: CIFAR accuracies 95.2/95.0/75.8/76.3 versus SGD 95.3/95.1/77.8/76.3, with three-run uncertainties. Its scalar step-size adaptation and constrained regularization distinguish it from coordinate-adaptive optimizers.

record.verdict_notes: SNLI Table 2 mixes new results with explicitly reused baselines. In particular, Adam and SGD results are reused, so their numerical comparison is not independent evidence from this study. No row IDs exist; verdicts therefore identify their textual evidence and corresponding missing results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy compared with natural-label performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Whether adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD under limited tuning, and stated recovery conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epochs and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and augmentation/regularization conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and its relation to train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10/100, WRN40-4 and DenseNet40-40; conventional adaptive optimizers versus scheduled SGD under the reported restricted tuning.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence, missing rows: Table 3 reports AMSGrad, AdamW and Yogi below SGD in all four settings, by 2.5–9.1 accuracy points; L4 variants also perform worse. Regularization and batch-size tuning extend beyond V4's narrow tuning condition.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored SGD over AMSGrad, AdamW, Yogi, and L4 variants, but these comparisons remain unverified and tuning extended to regularization and batch size.

relationships.reason: Text-only evidence, missing rows: Section 5.2 describes most adaptive methods as close to SGD; Adam and AMSGrad reach 97.9%, Adagrad 98.0%, and SGD 98.3%. The optimizer difference is small here.
relationships.display_finding: Reported SVHN accuracies place Adam, AMSGrad, and Adagrad close to SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ALI-G, which adapts a scalar learning rate while retaining SGD's descent direction.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence, missing rows: ALI-G reaches 98.1% versus SGD's 98.3% on SVHN, nearly matches SGD on CIFAR-10, and ties it at 76.3% on DenseNet/CIFAR-100; adaptive learning rates do not uniformly imply poor held-out performance.
relationships.display_finding: ALI-G reportedly performed close to SGD on SVHN and CIFAR-10 and matched SGD on DenseNet/CIFAR-100, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
